It is a public act (jure imperii). A minister's use of lethal force is an exercise of sovereign authority, and unlawfulness doesn't turn it into commercial (jure gestionis) activity (*Germany v. Italy*, ICJ 2012). Whether immunity still applies is a separate question, since it can be denied on other grounds, such as the territorial tort exception or the limits on immunity ratione materiae for international crimes.

CONFIDENCE: 80
